one_liner: Pure-Rust port of libjpeg-turbo with AVX2/NEON kernels that decodes a few percent faster than C on x86_64 and encodes at about C speed.
what_it_does: A full JPEG codec in Rust: baseline, progressive, arithmetic and lossless JPEG, 8/12/16-bit, every libjpeg subsampling mode, lossless transforms, crop and scaled decode, with output checked byte for byte against C libjpeg-turbo in CI. The Rust API is high-level (decompress, decompress_into, compress, an Encoder builder, ScanlineDecoder). The workspace also builds C ABI shims: a TurboJPEG 3 libturbojpeg.so.0 (the primary target) and an experimental classic libjpeg v8 libjpeg.so.8, so C and C++ programs can link it.
how_it_is_fast: It reimplements libjpeg-turbo's pipeline (Huffman decode, accurate integer IDCT, fancy upsampling, colour conversion) with hand-written AVX2/SSE2 intrinsics chosen by runtime CPUID dispatch and NEON on aarch64. Its own fused kernels go beyond C's, such as an AVX2 fancy H2V2 upsampler that does the vertical and horizontal triangle filters in one pass over 16 samples and a fused FDCT, quantize, colour and downsample encode path. The Huffman encoder skips zero coefficients with a bitmap using TZCNT/BLSR/LZCNT (BMI1/LZCNT) and has a runtime-dispatched BMI2 tier. The release profile uses fat LTO for cross-module inlining.
when_to_use: Rust services that decode many photo JPEGs of 320x240 and up on x86_64 with AVX2: the repo's own runs put decode at 0.83-0.98x of C libjpeg-turbo's time on an i5-10400.
You want libjpeg-turbo-identical output without a C toolchain: cross-compiling, wasm32 with SIMD128, or no_std + alloc firmware (thumbv7em is CI-built).
Replacing zune-jpeg in `image`-crate pipelines: the README reports 31 wins and 3 losses out of 34 decode cases on aarch64 and 1.31x faster through the image bridge at 1080p.
You need libjpeg features that lighter Rust decoders lack: progressive or arithmetic encode, lossless JPEG, 12/16-bit, DCT-coefficient access, lossless rotate/flip with marker copying.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ code that already links libjpeg-turbo: speed is at parity (M1 Pro decode 0.99-1.07x and encode 1.03-1.07x of C), and the C library is far more mature.
Encode-heavy x86_64 work on a portable (distro-style) build: 1.00-1.08x of C 3.2.0's time on a Zen 3 runner and 1.09-1.10x on Zen 4 at 1080p. The float DCT path trails C by 1.4-1.9x (issue #600).

Untrusted input where memory safety is the reason to choose Rust: the README makes no memory-safety guarantee while the unsafe SIMD boundary is audited, and issue #610 (open) is an out-of-bounds stack write reachable from safe Rust.

Tiny images (64x64 decodes 1.23x slower than C; 16x16 cases lose on fixed cost) and 32-bit ARM or RISC-V Vector hardware, where there is no SIMD backend and the README estimates 2-5x (armv7) and roughly 1.5-4x decode (RVV) slower than C.
As a system libjpeg.so.62 (v6b) or v7 replacement: the README says struct layouts differ and substitution corrupts memory; the v8 ABI is experimental.

integration.form: crate (plus cdylib C ABI shims: libturbojpeg.so.0 for TurboJPEG 3, experimental libjpeg.so.8)
integration.dependencies: thiserror; optional png crate behind the `png` feature; no C libraries
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.87 (MSRV, CI-enforced); the image-bridge crate needs 1.88
integration.platforms: x86_64 (AVX2/SSE2 runtime dispatch, Linux/macOS/Windows), aarch64 (NEON), wasm32 (SIMD128); scalar on RISC-V, POWER, s390x, armv7 and thumbv7em (no_std)
integration.thread_safety: Decoder is Send (installed marker callbacks must be Send, issue #384 per a source comment); the C ABI threading contract is in docs/ABI_COMPATIBILITY.md (not read)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the TurboJPEG 3 C ABI shim is the primary replacement target and the libjpeg v8 ABI is experimental; v6b/v7 ABIs are explicit non-goals, and the README itself makes no unqualified drop-in claim

gotchas: Issue #610 (open, 2026-09-08): Encoder::scan_script accepts a spectral end Se > 63. On x86_64 the SSE2 prepare_ac_first_sse2 path then writes about 272 bytes past two [u16; 64] stack arrays and returns Ok with corrupt output; aarch64 panics instead. Validate custom scan scripts yourself until it is fixed.

The newest crates.io release is 0.8.0 (2026-07-28), but the README's performance tables and the runtime BMI2/FMA dispatch come from main in September 2026. Pin a git revision if you need the measured code. Compile-time -C target-feature=+bmi2,+fma binaries fault on CPUs without those features.

The x86_64 decode table (i5-10400, C 3.1.2) does not state the rustc version or how the C library was built (the encode harness's build comment links a conda $CONDA_PREFIX libjpeg). Its best case, 0.77x at 320x240, looks like a C-side outlier: C's time there is 13.0 ns per pixel vs 10.8-11.3 ns at 1280x720 4:2:0 and 640x480 4:2:2 (derived from page data), and the repo's 2026-04-12 report on the same CPU measured 1.00x for that case.

The repo root carries committed benchmark binaries (bench_c_decode_matrix is a Mach-O arm64 build linked to Homebrew's libjpeg.8.dylib; bench_c_encode_linux is an x86-64 ELF). The C sides of the aarch64 tables used the classic libjpeg API, while the x86 decode harness (benches/c_baseline.c) used TurboJPEG tj3Decompress8.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is a port of libjpeg-turbo, so for C/C++ the original stays the default. Pick this one when a Rust or C-toolchain-free build needs libjpeg-turbo's exact output and full feature set at roughly equal speed. Compared with zenjpeg (faster Rust decode with different upsampling defaults) or the jpeg-nitro parallel decoders, it trades peak decode speed for bit-exact libjpeg-turbo compatibility and a TurboJPEG C ABI.
verified_claims_summary: Decode, first party: on an Intel i5-10400 (turbo off) a stock `cargo build --release` (fat LTO) decoded q75 fixtures in 0.87-0.97x of C libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2's time from 640x480 4:2:2 up to 3840x2160 and 0.77x at 320x240, but was slower at 64x64 (1.23x) and on the 640x480 gradient (1.05x). Both sides used the accurate integer IDCT and fancy upsampling (TurboJPEG FASTDCT=0, FASTUPSAMPLE=0; Rust defaults IsLow, merged upsampling off). The C loop reuses its output buffer while Rust's Criterion loop allocates one per decode. Encode is the only table with full methodology (rustc 1.98.1, official libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 .deb, cc -O2 harness, AMD EPYC 7763), and there Rust is slower at 1.00-1.08x of C.
status_note: Very active (last commit 2026-09-22, 1,759 commits, most recent ones co-authored with Claude), 9 GitHub stars but about 40k crates.io downloads (38.5k in the last 90 days), MIT OR Apache-2.0. 44 open issues, mostly C-ABI parity and unsafe-audit items, so treat the C ABI shims as pre-1.0.
